explain.say: Here is a riddle for you. An island is land with water all around it. Australia has water all around it too. So why do we call Australia a continent? Look at the bars to find out.

faq.q: What is the biggest island in the world?
faq.a: Greenland, about 2.17 million square kilometres. It is part of the Kingdom of Denmark, and about four fifths of it is covered by an ice sheet.

faq.q: Why is Australia a continent and not an island?
faq.a: Australia is much bigger than any island, more than three times Greenland, and it sits on its own tectonic plate. So geographers count it as a continent.
asks: Why is Australia not an island?

faq.q: Which island is shared by three countries?
faq.a: Borneo, in Southeast Asia. Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei all have land on it.

faq.q: Why is Greenland called Greenland if it is icy?
faq.a: A story says the Viking Erik the Red chose a pleasant name about a thousand years ago to make settlers want to go there. The southern coasts are green in summer.
An island is a piece of land, smaller than a continent, with water all around it.

facts: Greenland is the world's largest island, about 2.17 million square kilometres.
Borneo is the only island divided between three countries: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
